content:
The public result is a faithful receipt of the disclosed observation (matching stdout hex and passed=true), so the four fixed probes genuinely passed. My analysis of the candidate pattern against the contract yields the decisive defect:

- Pattern: `^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?[ \t]*$`
- The closing-group lookbehind `(?<=[ \t])` requires the character immediately before the closing run to be a space/tab. With non-greedy `text`, for any title whose last literal character is `#` (e.g. `C#`), the only position where the closing group could attach (immediately after the title) is blocked, and the regex cannot match at the terminal `#` positions either.
- Consequence: `# C#  ##` (attached hash followed by trailing whitespace plus a separate closing run — a case the task explicitly says must yield `C#`) yields title `C#  ##` instead of `C#`. The baseline would have returned `C#`. The four public cases don't cover this (the single-space `# C# #` works because the group can match just the final `#`).
- All other contract points hold: attached hashes literal (with trailing space, `# C# ` works; empty `# ##` works), levels/line numbers/`strip()`/fence/section/lookup code unchanged, and only the single authorized file changed.
